name: Tagmira
tagline: Hardscrabble upland village under the Bramblewood, holding off orcs it no longer understands.
ruler: No lord. The elders, with militia captain Hadran Throsk holding informal court in the hearth-hall.
faiths: Cossus (the stone circle; trial by combat)
Thulda (the gravefield and the Mound of Threads)
strangers: The party is known: owed for the northwest, and blamed for the dead. Hostility sits just under the surface.

far: the Bramblewood a dark mass on the horizon
threshold: a wooden palisade, not much of a wall
leaving: eyes on your back from the doorways

dusk: dogs going quiet near the forest edge
night: the Bramblewood black against the stars

day: goats and sheep in the lanes
dusk: wool and iron charms on the lintels
night: a lamp in every window facing north

spring: militia out on patrol to the northwest
autumn: hunters back from the northwest, fewer than before

situations.name: Cossial
descriptors: duels at the Circle of Cossus

situations.name: Thuldar
descriptors: wool laid on the Mound of Threads

situations.name: The autumn slaughter
descriptors: the whole village at the slaughter

itself.title: The dead walk
itself.text: Everyone knows the dead walk in the Bramblewood, and some of Tagmira's own recent dead have gone there. Doors are barred at dusk.

itself.title: Owed and blamed
itself.text: The party pushed the Bronze Host back and retook the northwestern hunting grounds, and the village will eat this winter because of it. Their alliance with the dead is known. Some are grateful; others blame them for the dead who walked into the wood.

itself.title: Black legs
itself.text: Whole legs of mutton and goat are salted and cold-smoked for months over ridge juniper at Carnaxe. Black legs are the local delicacy and the reason caravans stop. Hunters' hams of venison and boar cost more. Blood sausage is eaten fresh at the autumn slaughter and never sold; a visitor offered some is being honoured.

itself.title: Sacred ground everywhere
itself.text: A Cossus stone ring for trial by combat, a Thulda gravefield, a mound of wool offerings, an Isarna waystone, and a ford whose cold shrine is being restored. The village keeps them all.

day: **Hadran Throsk** wants news of the northwest.
Hunters back from the northwest with a full haul nod to the party.
**Tenn Darnel** glares at **Ulan Caernach** across a field boundary.
A widow spits at the party's feet; her husband walked into the Bramblewood.
**1d3 militia** practise with bows behind the hearth-hall.
A cart of black legs comes down from Carnaxe, wrapped in sacking.
night: The dogs at the forest edge stop barking all at once.
**Old Borric** swears to anyone listening that he saw Maedra on the Bramblewood path.
**2 militia** on the palisade, watching the northwest.
A figure stands at the edge of the Bramblewood until a lantern is raised.
A family keeps vigil over a fresh body, axes ready.

response.reinforcements: 6 veterans, including Borric and Feln. The hunters, about a dozen, may come or may not; they answer to no one.
response.strength_now: 7 militia, 6 veterans, and a dozen hunters outside the militia
response.strength: Seasoned now. They fought beside the party, won the northwest back, and sleep badly anyway.

locations.name: Hearth-Hall
locations.look: The central gathering hall: food, drink, and village business.

labels.guests: Villagers and militia; Hadran Throsk holds informal court most evenings.

locations.name: The Crescent and Hoof
locations.look: The caravan inn on the west road, near where Taziri's route ends.

labels.sign: A crescent over a hoofprint, copied from the Isarna waystone.
labels.common_room: Long tables around a fire pit, with teamsters' boots drying beside it.
labels.guests: Taziri's teamsters, pony buyers, and the odd pilgrim to the waystone.
labels.services: Private rooms (4), common floor, meals, stabling. Smoked mutton and goat cheese. Prices pending OSRIC 3.0 table.
labels.trouble: Teamsters talk. Whatever the caravan heard on the road, the village knows by morning.

locations.name: The Barred Door
locations.look: A low drinking-house where the hunters drink.

labels.sign: None. Three iron bars are nailed across the door, put up the week the dead walked.
labels.common_room: Low and smoky, with one long bench and tallow lamps.
labels.guests: Hunters, woodcutters, off-duty militia, and the ones who blame the party.
labels.services: Ale; bread and dripping; floor space. Prices pending OSRIC 3.0 table.
labels.trouble: The party is served, slowly. Someone always brings up the Bramblewood dead.

locations.name: Circle of Cossus
locations.look: A stone ring in a forest glade south of the village, consecrated to Cossus.

labels.interior: The stones hum faintly when oaths are spoken.

locations.name: Gravefield of Thulda
locations.look: Burial mounds northeast of the village, ringed by carved posts and wrapped in wool.

labels.populace: Two quiet widows tend the mounds.

locations.name: Mound of Threads
locations.look: A rounded earthen mound on the western ridge, both tomb and shrine to Thulda.

locations.name: Tree of Mist-Song
locations.look: A lightning-scarred ash on a stony knoll north of the village, one of the oldest trees in the region.

labels.custom: Stones carved with spirals and claw marks ring its roots.

locations.hidden: A dryad is trapped in the tree, dormant from loneliness. She stirs for real druidic attention, or for someone who sits by the tree in silence for a full turn.

locations.name: Waystone of Isarna
locations.look: A stone marker etched with a crescent and a hoofprint, on the road west of the village.

labels.custom: Travellers leave bread and silver thread.

locations.name: Ford of Ossamar
locations.look: A wide, clear ford three miles east, marked by cairns and iron braziers.

labels.passage: Usable. Meria of the Ford has come from Lamares to restore the shrine, cold since Ildun-Ayenar was taken.

locations.name: Palisade
locations.look: A wooden palisade around the village.

labels.watch: Not fortified; a serious assault would be catastrophic.

locations.name: The Ash-House
locations.look: Enni's turf-roofed lean-to at the edge of the western woods, smoke leaking through the thatch.

labels.inhabitants: Enni the Ash-Wife and her servant Medam.

locations.hidden: A hearth-pit of ash many years deep, with small bones in it.

locations.name: The Wheel-Ring
locations.look: A churned yard beside the Crescent and Hoof where Taziri's route ends.

labels.yard: Wagons drawn up in a ring at night.

locations.name: Caturo's Corrals
locations.look: Rail fences on the south slope.

labels.wares: Hardy upland ponies, the village's best export.

labels.proprietor: Tarrek Veyran and his apprentices, Garrin and Felmar.

locations.name: Corr's Chandlery
locations.look: The tallow-house, set downwind of the village.

labels.wares: Tallow and candles rendered from sheep fat.

locations.name: Tanning Pits
locations.look: Pits by the stream below the village.

factions.purpose: Keep the orcs cowed and the village fed.
factions.scheme: Hold the retaken northwest hunting grounds.

factions.purpose: Feed the village and keep the northwest.
factions.membership: About a dozen hunters, Cael Gald among them.
factions.scheme: Hunt the far grounds without the militia's leave, and sell the game to Carnaxe.

trouble: The Bronze Host was pushed back from the northwest, but all its leaders survived.
The party's alliance with the dead is known, and resented by some; a few blame the party for the dead who went to the Bramblewood.
Maedra has vanished — whispers but no answers. The undead want more Tagmiran recruits.

Two Bronze Host orcs were brought to Tagmira as captives to witness the trial by combat — meant as intimidation. It may have given the orcs useful intelligence about Tagmira's current strength instead.
The water-rights grudge persists after the duel. Tenn Darnel lost and has not forgiven Ulan Caernach.
Ulan Caernach and Rondasek Elaran are back to village life but changed — they've seen skeletons fight and orcs bleed. They are quietly restless.
Salt comes only by caravan. Taziri, Aelis Varrow, and the Aredos haggle over it every curing season.
The militia resents the Aredos buying game from the hunters, off grounds the militia bled to retake.

legacy_rumours: Old Maedra walked into the Bramblewood one night and didn't come back. Some say she went to die in peace. Others say the wood took her.
Old Borric swears he saw Maedra on the Bramblewood path at dusk — but she looked wrong. He won't say how.
The Ford of Ossamar has gone cold since Ildun vanished. Offerings left there feel unaccepted.

waystone_stop.location: Waystone of Isarna, west of Tagmira (on the road from Caelrun)
waystone_stop.event: Taziri will want to stop for an offering. Bread and silver thread are traditional. Good moment for character roleplay and transition into Tagmira.
waystone_stop.dm_notes: Let this breathe — it signals arrival is near and gives the caravan a moment of ritual normalcy before the complications of Tagmira begin.

flavor_notes: The road north narrows. The Bramblewood is visible as a dark mass on the horizon well before Tagmira itself.
Taziri knows Tagmira well — she can brief the party on surface village politics if asked.
The militia members who know the party might be met on the road or at the gate.
Nothing in the Bramblewood moves by day — but the sense of being watched from the tree line is hard to shake.

possible_road_encounter.name: Returning Patrol
possible_road_encounter.description: A Tagmira patrol of 3 militia heading back from the northwest. They are not fleeing — they held the line but were outmatched. One is bandaged. They know the party and will report directly: the orcs have bronze weapons, they move in coordinated groups, and there are more of them than last spring. They want to know if the party is coming to help.
possible_road_encounter.dm_notes: Sets the tone correctly — these are not frightened villagers, they are soldiers who fought and are thinking about how to fight better. The party's arrival matters to them.

immediate: Zimru wants an accounting of the sacrifice and a commitment to the next one — the orcs northwest are the obvious candidates
Tagmira's hunters are being pushed off the northwest grounds — Hadran needs help or intelligence
Maedra's transformation — the party will face her changed, and the village still doesn't know she's gone
slow_burn: The undead want Tagmiran recruits — someone in the village may already be in contact with them
The dryad in the Tree of Mist-Song — bitterly lonely, has knowledge of the Bramblewood, waiting
Velric's warning from the Sphere — a great danger foreseen, not yet revealed
Tenn Darnel lost the duel and has not forgiven it — a grudge waiting for a trigger
session_pressure_points.convergence: The orc threat and the sacrifice demand point in the same direction — the party can satisfy Zimru and defend Tagmira with the same action, if they can coordinate militia, manage the undead alliance's secrecy, and get through the Bronze Host's now-upgraded defenses.

outside_powers.name: Temple of the Old Gods (Zimru's undead)
outside_powers.current_posture: Quiet and patient. Sphere is functional after the orc sacrifice. Want more sacrifices — specifically more orcs, which conveniently aligns with Tagmira's orc problem. Also quietly seeking Tagmiran 'recruits' for undeath. Maedra is now Zimru's consort and seen by the undead as nearly a prophet.
outside_powers.disposition_to_party: Allied, with expectations. Zimru will want an accounting of the sacrifice and will press for the next one.
outside_powers.party_terms: The party accepts Ildun-Ayenar's sacrifice but forbids more human ones. Orcs and other humanoids only.

outside_powers.name: Bronze Host (Pact-Render orcs)
outside_powers.location: Northwest hunting grounds and the Bronzeworking Triangle beyond
outside_powers.current_posture: Actively pushing Tagmirans out of the northwest forest. Two months since the raid — all named orc leaders survived, equipment upgraded via Pact-Render fey bronze. Making a play for the hunting grounds as first step toward assault on Tagmira proper. The undead know and cannot act.

militia_members.name: Village Militia
militia_members.strength: 7 standing, 6 veterans who can be called
members: Torven Gald — lanky archer raised among woodsmen. Talks too much. Deadly accurate. Wants a reputation; oddly, also a wayhouse of his own.
Kerrig Bronn — broad-shouldered veteran from the northern hills. Speaks little, watches much. Wants his sons safe; will not lead again.
militia_members.awareness_of_undead: Dim — they know something is wrong in the Bramblewood, have heard stories, but have no clear picture
militia_members.awareness_of_orc_threat: High — the Bronze Host has been pushing hunters out of the northwest grounds for two months
militia_members.disposition_to_party: Favorable — the party fought alongside them against the orc raid
militia_members.character: Not a garrison force — Tagmirans are tough and have always spent the spring patrolling and intimidating the orcs. They know what war costs. The problem is not their courage but that the Bronze Host has suddenly become something different: better equipped, coordinated, and backed by something the militia does not understand.
militia_members.spring_patrol_tradition: Every spring the militia patrols the northwest aggressively to keep orc pressure down. This has worked for a generation. It is not working now.

ford_of_ossamar.current_state: Abandoned since the undead abducted Ildun-Ayenar here and carried him to the Temple of the Old Gods, where he was sacrificed to power the Sphere. The ford is still usable but the sacred atmosphere has drained away.
ford_of_ossamar.dm_notes: The party accepts Ildun's sacrifice, on one condition: no more humans. Orcs and other humanoids only. Villagers think Ildun wandered off or died quietly. Anyone who knew him well — Maedra did — carries the truth into undeath.

circle_of_cossus.current_state: The stones still hum faintly when oaths are spoken. The fey corruption is old and dormant but not gone.
circle_of_cossus.dm_notes: Sardet's officiating here is remembered. If the party needs to call in goodwill with Tagmira, this is a touchstone. The residual fey taint is undetectable except to a druid (Brigantios could sense it). It is old and dormant but not gone.

mound_of_threads.dm_notes: No supernatural activity here yet, but Thulda's domain is death and mourning — thematically resonant with everything happening at the temple.

tree_of_mist_song.current_state: The dryad is present but dormant from loneliness and despair. She will respond to genuine druidic attention or to someone who sits with her tree in true silence for a full turn.
tree_of_mist_song.dm_notes: Once roused she will be desperate and raw — centuries of isolation. She knows things about the Bramblewood's origins (it was seeded by the old gods as a perimeter). Could become an ally or a tragedy depending on the party's choices. Nabia, Bracara's mentor, once held vigil here.

waystone_of_isarna.current_state: Active and well-maintained by passing travelers.
waystone_of_isarna.dm_notes: Good moment for roleplay as the caravan arrives. Taziri's offering here is a natural transition into Tagmira proper.

bramblewood.current_state: The orc Bronze Host is pressing from the northwest. The undead are aware but cannot project force outside the Bramblewood. The party is caught between these pressures.
bramblewood.dm_notes: See temple and orc sections below.

bramblewood.description: The dense thorn-forest north of Tagmira. Grown by the old gods as a living perimeter, seeded with divine fear and watered by clerics' blood (see Thorn-Bound Covenant). Contains the Temple of the Old Gods. The undead cannot stray far from it without losing consciousness unless they pay a high magical cost.

bramblewood.dm_notes: See temple and orc sections below.
